title: Mittag–Leffler cohomology for constant reductions on a weakly contractible affine
statement: Let $W$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] that is weakly contractible for its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], meaning that evaluation at the final object takes every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $J\subseteq A$ an ideal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived tensor [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $H\in D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\underline A)$ be locally derived $J\underline A$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. Put $H_n=H\otimes_A^L\underline{A/J^n}$ with their canonical quotient transitions. Assume that for every $n\geq1$ there is $E_n\in D(A/J^n)$ and an isomorphism $H_n\simeq\underline{E_n}$, and that $E_1$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Then for every integer $q$ the inverse sequence of hypercohomology groups $H^q(W,H_n)$ is Mittag–Leffler: for each $n$ there is $m\geq n$ such that the images of $H^q(W,H_k)\to H^q(W,H_n)$ are equal for all $k\geq m$. Here hypercohomology is the cohomology of derived sections, as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The isomorphisms $H_n\simeq\underline{E_n}$ are not assumed compatible with the transition maps. No quotient $A/J^n$ is assumed finite as a set.

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-triple-range-ml-transfer] to its two comparison equations. This is exactly the proof in the Lean module; the geometric and algebraic subarguments now belong to the finite-comparison dependency.

lean.statement: theorem wcontractible_constant_reductions_mittagLeffler (W : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine W] (_hW : ∀ (F G : Sheaf (ProEt.topology W) (Type (u + 1))) (f : F ⟶ G), Epi f → Function.Surjective (f.hom.app (op (⊤_ W.ProEt)))) (A : Type (max v (u + 1))) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (J : Ideal A) (H : ConstantCompletion.D (ConstantCompletion.constant (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} W) A)) (_hcomplete : ConstantCompletion.IsComplete (ConstantCompletion.quotient (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} W) A J 0) H) (_hconstant : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ E : MLAlgebraDerived (A ⧸ J ^ (n + 1)), (n = 0 → MLAlgebraPerfect E) ∧ Nonempty ((ConstantCompletion.extend (ConstantCompletion.quotient (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} W) A J n)).obj H ≅ mlConstantDerivedObject W (A ⧸ J ^ (n + 1)) E)) : ∀ q : ℤ, (mlHypercohomologyTower W A J H q).IsMittagLeffler
lean.note: Uses the existing coefficient-sized small pro-etale model coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} (def-weil-proetale-inverse-image), standard derived localizations, exact constant-module realization and the published universally normalized strict quotient tower. The coefficient ring lives in Type (max v (u + 1)), the same convention as the citer lem-sfb-adic-residue-lisse-perfect-lift; the reviewer generalized the delivered Type (u + 1) (proEtaleModelTopology) form, which forced the coefficient universe to equal the site universe. Index n denotes exponent n+1. Completeness is the existing local internal-Hom condition for the kernel of the actual residue quotient. Hypercohomology is computed by exact final-object sections after cohomology on this weakly contractible site; no finite quotient or coherent marking hypothesis is imposed.
